components.note: 巴 (bā) — 巴 gives the sound bā in 爸 bà, 吧 ba, 把 bǎ and 疤 bā, so it is a useful sound clue.
斤 (axe) — the original idea was chopping with an axe, as in 新, 斩 chop, 断 break; today 斯 is mostly a sound-borrowing syllable sī in foreign names like 俄罗斯.

example.hanzi: 巴斯是英国西南部一座著名的古城。
example.pinyin: Bāsī shì Yīngguó xīnánbù yí zuò zhùmíng de gǔchéng.
example.english: Bath is a famous ancient city in southwest England.
example.fact: The city of Bath is named for its natural hot springs, the only ones in Britain, which the Romans channeled into an elaborate bathing complex around 70 AD that still stands today as the Roman Baths. The springs draw water heated deep underground that resurfaces at about 46 degrees Celsius, having taken an estimated 10,000 years to complete its journey through the rock.

examples.hanzi: 去英国旅行时，我们顺便参观了巴斯。
examples.pinyin: Qù Yīngguó lǚxíng shí, wǒmen shùnbiàn cānguān le Bāsī.
examples.english: On our trip to England, we visited Bath along the way.

examples.hanzi: 巴斯以古罗马浴场闻名。
examples.pinyin: Bāsī yǐ gǔ Luómǎ yùchǎng wénmíng.
examples.english: Bath is famous for its ancient Roman baths.

components.note: 米 (rice, grain) — 米 is rice and grain, as in 粥, 糖, 精; 粉 is flour ground from grain, then powder.
分 (fēn) — same sound, different tone — 粉 is fěn; 分 also sounds out 份 fèn.

example.hanzi: 她喜欢穿粉色的裙子。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan chuān fěnsè de qúnzi.
example.english: She likes to wear pink skirts.
example.fact: 粉 means powder, then 'pink' (粉色,粉红) and rice or starch noodles (米粉). 粉丝 is a famous double meaning: it is both 'vermicelli' and the transliteration of 'fans', so 我是他的粉丝 means 'I'm his fan'.

examples.hanzi: 请帮我把药粉倒进水里。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ bǎ yàofěn dào jìn shuǐ li.
examples.english: Please help me pour the powdered medicine into the water.

examples.hanzi: 我午饭吃了一碗米粉。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ wǔfàn chī le yì wǎn mǐfěn.
examples.english: I had a bowl of rice noodles for lunch.

components.note: 火 (fire) — 火 is fire, as in 烧, 灯, 炒; 灭 covers a fire with a stroke 一 to put it out.

example.hanzi: 风一吹，蜡烛就灭了。
example.pinyin: Fēng yì chuī, làzhú jiù miè le.
example.english: The candle went out as soon as the wind blew.
example.fact: 灭 can describe flames or lights going out (灯灭了) and 'to destroy' in 消灭 and 灭绝 (extinction). 灭火 means to put out a fire, and 灭火器 is a fire extinguisher.

examples.hanzi: 消防员很快把火扑灭了。
examples.pinyin: Xiāofángyuán hěn kuài bǎ huǒ pūmiè le.
examples.english: The firefighters soon put out the fire.

examples.hanzi: 这种动物已经灭绝了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng dòngwù yǐjīng mièjué le.
examples.english: This species is already extinct.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — speech and talk: 说, 论, 请; 评 is to comment and judge.
平 (píng) sounds exactly like 评; also in 苹 píng.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 估 is a trader's guess at value.
古 (gǔ) is a close sound clue; same part in 姑 gū, 枯 kū, 苦 kǔ.

example.hanzi: 专家对这个项目的风险进行了评估。
example.pinyin: Zhuānjiā duì zhège xiàngmù de fēngxiǎn jìnxíng le pínggū.
example.english: Experts carried out a risk assessment of this project.
example.fact: The Richter scale, long used to assess earthquake magnitude, is logarithmic, meaning each whole-number increase represents a tenfold rise in measured amplitude and roughly 31 times more released energy. Because of this, seismologists now more often rely on the moment magnitude scale for large earthquakes, which better assesses total energy release for the biggest, most damaging events.

examples.hanzi: 银行会评估你的还款能力。
examples.pinyin: Yínháng huì pínggū nǐ de huánkuǎn nénglì.
examples.english: The bank will assess your ability to repay.

examples.hanzi: 这份评估报告明天就能出来。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn pínggū bàogào míngtiān jiù néng chūlái.
examples.english: This assessment report will be ready tomorrow.

components.note: 角 (horn) — an ox's horn; with 刀 (knife) the picture is cutting up an ox, so "to take apart", then to loosen and explain.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 分, 切, 到; a blade separates the parts.
阝 on the left is 阜 (steps, hill) — as in 院, 阳, 阴: 除 first meant palace steps; to step away, remove.
余 (yú) is a loose sound clue for chú; 余 also in 涂 tú, 途 tú and 徐 xú.

example.hanzi: 政府决定解除对该地区的旅行限制。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ juédìng jiěchú duì gāi dìqū de lǔxíng xiànzhì.
example.english: The government decided to lift travel restrictions on the region.
example.fact: The United States lifted its arms embargo against Vietnam in 2016, more than 40 years after the end of the Vietnam War, as part of a broader normalization of relations between the two countries. Embargoes of this kind are typically removed gradually, often tied to specific diplomatic or human rights benchmarks rather than a single decision.

examples.hanzi: 台风警报已经解除了。
examples.pinyin: Táifēng jǐngbào yǐjīng jiěchú le.
examples.english: The typhoon warning has been lifted.

examples.hanzi: 公司和他解除了劳动合同。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī hé tā jiěchú le láodòng hétong.
examples.english: The company terminated his employment contract.

components.note: 车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.
广 (building) — marks halls and shelters, as in 店, 座, 床; 库 is a storehouse, here for carts 车.

example.hanzi: 他把车停在车库里。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ chē tíng zài chēkù lǐ.
example.english: He parked the car in the garage.
example.fact: The Hewlett-Packard company was founded in a one-car garage in Palo Alto in 1939 by Bill Hewlett and David Packard, working with just $538 in starting capital. That garage is now a California Historical Landmark, often called the symbolic birthplace of Silicon Valley, since it set a pattern later followed by companies like Apple and Google, which also started in garages.

examples.hanzi: 我们家的车库可以停两辆车。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jiā de chēkù kěyǐ tíng liǎng liàng chē.
examples.english: Our garage can hold two cars.

examples.hanzi: 爸爸在车库里修自行车。
examples.pinyin: Bàba zài chēkù lǐ xiū zìxíngchē.
examples.english: Dad is fixing a bicycle in the garage.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: a way through.
甬 (yǒng) is a close sound clue for tōng; 甬 also in 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng and 勇 yǒng.
讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talk and news, as in 说, 话, 讲; 讯 is a message or an inquiry.
卂 (xùn) gives the sound exactly: 讯 xùn, also in 迅 xùn.

example.hanzi: 这家公司主要从事通讯设备的生产。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī zhǔyào cóngshì tōngxùn shèbèi de shēngchǎn.
example.english: This company mainly produces communications equipment.
example.fact: The first transatlantic telegraph cable, completed in 1858, cut communication time between North America and Europe from about ten days by ship to just minutes, though the cable itself failed after only a few weeks due to a technical fault. A more durable cable was successfully laid in 1866, permanently transforming global communications and finance by allowing near-instant transatlantic messages.

examples.hanzi: 山里的通讯信号很差。
examples.pinyin: Shān lǐ de tōngxùn xìnhào hěn chà.
examples.english: The communication signal in the mountains is poor.

examples.hanzi: 这篇通讯报道了灾区的最新情况。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān tōngxùn bàodào le zāiqū de zuìxīn qíngkuàng.
examples.english: This news report covers the latest situation in the disaster area.

components.note: 日 (sun) — time and day, as in 时, 晚, 明: the sun at the top of a sprout, early morning. 早 also gives 草 cǎo and 澡 zǎo.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.

example.hanzi: 他每天早上都会跟邻居说一声早安。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān zǎoshang dōu huì gēn línjū shuō yìshēng zǎo'ān.
example.english: Every morning he greets his neighbor with a 'good morning.'
example.fact: Human circadian rhythms, which govern when we naturally wake and feel alert, are regulated by a small cluster of about 20,000 neurons in the brain called the suprachiasmatic nucleus, which resets daily based on light hitting the eyes. This is why morning sunlight exposure is one of the most effective tools for adjusting sleep schedules, including recovering from jet lag.

examples.hanzi: 早安，今天天气真好！
examples.pinyin: Zǎo'ān, jīntiān tiānqì zhēn hǎo!
examples.english: Good morning, the weather is lovely today!

examples.hanzi: 她每天都会给我发一条早安的消息。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi tiān dōu huì gěi wǒ fā yì tiáo zǎo'ān de xiāoxi.
examples.english: She sends me a good morning message every day.

components.note: ⺈ (bent figure) — top part, a person; with 口 and 儿 it forms 免. Origin unclear; Memory aid: a person with a hat slipping out, 'excused'.
儿 (legs) — the bottom part and radical, a walking person, as in 先 first and 兄 older brother.

example.hanzi: 学生可以免费参观。
example.pinyin: Xuésheng kěyǐ miǎnfèi cānguān.
example.english: Students can visit for free.
example.fact: 免 is the word behind 免费 (free of charge), 免税 (duty-free) and 难免 (hard to avoid). 免得 and 省得 both mean 'so as not to', as in 带把伞，免得淋雨 ('take an umbrella so you won't get wet').

examples.hanzi: 孩子身高一米以下免票。
examples.pinyin: Háizi shēngāo yì mǐ yǐxià miǎnpiào.
examples.english: Children under one meter tall get in free.

examples.hanzi: 为了避免迟到,我早点出门。
examples.pinyin: Wèile bìmiǎn chídào, wǒ zǎodiǎn chūmén.
examples.english: To avoid being late, I'm leaving early.

components.note: 身 (body) — a person's body with a rounded belly. As a radical it marks body words: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躯 body.
后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).

example.hanzi: 他身后留下了一笔可观的财产。
example.pinyin: Tā shēnhòu liúxià le yì bǐ kěguān de cáichǎn.
example.english: He left behind a considerable fortune after his death.
example.fact: Ancient Egyptian pharaohs were buried with elaborate provisions meant to last for the afterlife, including furniture, food, and in some cases entire boats, based on a belief that the journey continued after death. Tutankhamun's tomb, discovered largely intact in 1922, contained over 5,000 objects, giving archaeologists an unusually complete picture of what a ruler was thought to need beyond life.

examples.hanzi: 有人在我身后叫我的名字。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu rén zài wǒ shēnhòu jiào wǒ de míngzi.
examples.english: Someone behind me called my name.

examples.hanzi: 小狗一直跟在主人身后。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu yìzhí gēn zài zhǔrén shēnhòu.
examples.english: The little dog keeps following behind its owner.

components.note: 日 (sun) — time and day, as in 时, 晚, 明: the sun at the top of a sprout, early morning. 早 also gives 草 cǎo and 澡 zǎo.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 他没时间吃早点就出门了。
example.pinyin: Tā méi shíjiān chī zǎodiǎn jiù chūmén le.
example.english: He left the house without time to eat breakfast.
example.fact: The word 'breakfast' literally describes breaking an overnight fast, and for most of human history, the meal was far less standardized than it is today — medieval European physicians sometimes even discouraged eating first thing in the morning, believing it disrupted digestion. It only became a widely promoted, regular meal in the 19th century, partly through advertising campaigns for new packaged foods like breakfast cereal.

examples.hanzi: 楼下的早点摊有豆浆和油条。
examples.pinyin: Lóuxià de zǎodiǎn tān yǒu dòujiāng hé yóutiáo.
examples.english: The breakfast stall downstairs sells soy milk and fried dough sticks.

examples.hanzi: 你早点吃了吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zǎodiǎn chī le ma?
examples.english: Have you had breakfast?

components.note: 皿 (dish) — marks vessels, as in 盒 box, 盖 lid, 盆 basin; 盘 is a plate.
舟 (boat) here stands in for 般 (bān), which hints at pán, as in 搬 bān.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 服务员端来了一盘子水果。
example.pinyin: Fúwùyuán duān lái le yì pánzi shuǐguǒ.
example.english: The waiter brought over a plate of fruit.
example.fact: Blue and white porcelain plates, closely associated with Chinese ceramics, reached peak popularity during the Yuan and Ming dynasties starting in the 14th century, using cobalt pigment imported along trade routes from Persia. European potters spent centuries trying to replicate true porcelain's hard, translucent quality, only succeeding after Johann Friedrich Böttger's breakthrough in Saxony in 1708.

examples.hanzi: 吃完饭，我帮妈妈洗盘子。
examples.pinyin: Chī wán fàn, wǒ bāng māma xǐ pánzi.
examples.english: After the meal, I help Mom wash the dishes.

examples.hanzi: 这个盘子是白色的，上面画着小花。
examples.pinyin: Zhège pánzi shì báisè de, shàngmiàn huà zhe xiǎo huā.
examples.english: This plate is white with little flowers painted on it.

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks slopes, as in 阶 steps, 院, 陆; 降 is to go down a slope.
夅 (two feet going down) — shows descent, and gives the sound: 降 jiàng.

example.hanzi: 明天气温会下降。
example.pinyin: Míngtiān qìwēn huì xiàjiàng.
example.english: The temperature will drop tomorrow.
example.fact: 降 has two readings: jiàng is 'to fall or lower' (降价, 降落, 降温) and xiáng is 'to surrender' (投降). The two are written the same, so watch the context.

examples.hanzi: 飞机慢慢降落了。
examples.pinyin: Fēijī mànmàn jiàngluò le.
examples.english: The plane slowly landed.

examples.hanzi: 商店的价格降了不少。
examples.pinyin: Shāngdiàn de jiàgé jiàng le bù shǎo.
examples.english: Prices at the shop have dropped quite a bit.

meanings: comes at the end of the sentence to indicate a strong degree

components.note: 著 (zhù / zhe) — older form of 着: 艹 plant + 者 (zhě) as sound. 着 is a variant with 羊 over 目; neither part gives the 'in progress' sense.
目 (eye) — the bottom. The eye family: 看, 眼, 睛, 睡. In 着 it is only part of a variant shape. Memory aid: 睡着 — eyes 目 shut, asleep.
口 (mouth) — marks speech and spoken particles, as in 吗, 吧, 啊; 呢 is a question or emphasis particle.
尼 (ní) gives the sound: 呢 ne/ní, also in 泥 ní.

example.hanzi: 这道题他其实明白着呢。
example.pinyin: Zhè dào tí tā qíshí míngbai zhe ne.
example.english: He actually understands this problem quite well.
example.fact: Emphatic sentence particles that intensify a statement appear in many of the world's languages, not just Chinese — Japanese uses particles like 'yo' and 'zo' for a similar effect, and colloquial German relies heavily on 'doch' and 'ja' to shade the emotional weight of a sentence. Linguists classify these as modal particles, since they change how strongly or in what tone a statement is meant, without altering its literal content.

examples.hanzi: 别小看他，他厉害着呢。
examples.pinyin: Bié xiǎokàn tā, tā lìhai zhene.
examples.english: Don't underestimate him; he's quite impressive.

examples.hanzi: 离放假还早着呢，再坚持一下。
examples.pinyin: Lí fàngjià hái zǎo zhene, zài jiānchí yíxià.
examples.english: There's still plenty of time before the holiday, so hang in there.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family terms, as in 妈 mom, 好 good, 姐 sister; 女 (nǚ) also loosely echoes the rú sound.
口 (mouth) — speech; 如 originally meant "to follow, accord with", later "as, like"; also in 汝 rǔ and 茹 rú.
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.

example.hanzi: 他的经历如同一部精彩的小说。
example.pinyin: Tā de jīnglì rútóng yí bù jīngcǎi de xiǎoshuō.
example.english: His experiences are just like an exciting novel.
example.fact: The chambered nautilus grows its spiral shell in a logarithmic pattern, adding new, proportionally larger chambers as it ages while always maintaining the same overall shape — a growth pattern often compared to certain hurricanes and galaxies because all three follow similar spiral mathematics. This is why the nautilus shell is a favorite classroom example for demonstrating logarithmic spirals found throughout nature.

examples.hanzi: 这里的春天如同画一样美。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de chūntiān rútóng huà yíyàng měi.
examples.english: Spring here is as beautiful as a painting.

examples.hanzi: 她对我如同亲妹妹一样。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì wǒ rútóng qīn mèimei yíyàng.
examples.english: She treats me just like a real younger sister.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 线, 组; 给 is to supply thread, then to give.
合 (hé) is only a loose sound clue; same part in 答 dá, 拾 shí, 恰 qià.
予 (yǔ) — to give; as a part it sounds out 预 yù, 野 yě and 序 xù.

example.hanzi: 公司决定给予员工额外的奖金。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī juédìng jǐyǔ yuángōng éwài de jiǎngjīn.
example.english: The company decided to give employees an extra bonus.
example.fact: The Nobel Prizes, among the most prestigious awards given for contributions to humanity, were established through the 1895 will of Swedish inventor Alfred Nobel, who left over 94 percent of his fortune to fund them — reportedly influenced by seeing himself mistakenly described in an obituary as a 'merchant of death' for inventing dynamite. The physics, chemistry, and medicine prizes have been awarded almost every year since 1901.

examples.hanzi: 感谢大家给予我的帮助。
examples.pinyin: Gǎnxiè dàjiā jǐyǔ wǒ de bāngzhù.
examples.english: Thank you all for the help you gave me.

examples.hanzi: 老师给予了他很高的评价。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī jǐyǔ le tā hěn gāo de píngjià.
examples.english: The teacher gave him high praise.

components.note: 廴 (long stride) — a rare radical of walking and extending, also in 延 yán and 廷 tíng; 建 means to set up or put up; the sound clue 聿 is only loose.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 造 is to go and make something.
告 (gào) is a loose sound clue (-ao); also in 浩 hào, 靠 kào.

example.hanzi: 工人们正在建造一座新桥。
example.pinyin: Gōngrénmen zhèngzài jiànzào yí zuò xīn qiáo.
example.english: The workers are building a new bridge.
example.fact: The Great Wall of China was not built as a single continuous project but assembled and rebuilt over roughly 2,000 years by successive dynasties, with the best-preserved sections dating to the Ming dynasty starting in the 14th century. Combining all its branches and sections, surveys have measured the wall's total length at more than 21,000 kilometers, far longer than the commonly cited figure for any single stretch.

examples.hanzi: 这座大桥建造了整整三年。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò dàqiáo jiànzào le zhěngzhěng sān nián.
examples.english: This big bridge took a full three years to build.

examples.hanzi: 他们打算在海边建造一座小别墅。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen dǎsuàn zài hǎibiān jiànzào yí zuò xiǎo biéshù.
examples.english: They plan to build a small villa by the sea.

components.note: 典 — a book 冊 set on a stand 丌, a revered text; hence canon, classic, as in 经典 classic and 字典 dictionary.
土 (earth) — 土 is earth, as in 地, 城; a mold was made of clay, so 型 is a model or type.
刑 (xíng) — same sound — 型 is xíng, like 刑.

example.hanzi: 这是一个典型的误解案例。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè diǎnxíng de wùjiě ànlì.
example.english: This is a typical case of misunderstanding.
example.fact: In biology, a 'type specimen' is the single physical example — often a preserved animal or plant — permanently designated as the official reference for a species' name, kept in a museum collection so scientists can compare future finds against it. Carl Linnaeus, who founded the modern system of naming species in the 18th century, based many of his original type specimens on collections that are still preserved today.

examples.hanzi: 他是个典型的北方人，说话很爽快。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gè diǎnxíng de běifāngrén, shuōhuà hěn shuǎngkuai.
examples.english: He is a typical northerner who speaks very frankly.

examples.hanzi: 这位老师是全校的先进典型。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎoshī shì quánxiào de xiānjìn diǎnxíng.
examples.english: This teacher is a model example for the whole school.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech and breath, as in 吃, 叫, 喝; 呵 is a laugh or a breath out.
可 (kě) hints at the sound: 呵 hē is close, and 可 also gives 河 hé, 歌 gē and 何 hé.
口 (mouth) — marks speech and breath, as in 吃, 叫, 喝; 呵 is a laugh or a breath out.
可 (kě) hints at the sound: 呵 hē is close, and 可 also gives 河 hé, 歌 gē and 何 hé.

example.hanzi: 他只是呵呵地笑了两声，没有说话。
example.pinyin: Tā zhǐshì hēhē de xiào le liǎng shēng, méiyǒu shuōhuà.
example.english: He just chuckled softly and didn't say anything.
example.fact: Laughter is thought to have evolved long before spoken language, since chimpanzees and other great apes produce a breathy, panting vocalization during play that researchers consider an evolutionary precursor to human laughing. Human laughter itself splits into distinct types studied by acoustic researchers, ranging from voiced, song-like laughs to unvoiced grunts and chuckles, each carrying different social signals.

examples.hanzi: 老爷爷呵呵地笑着，摸了摸孩子的头。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo yéye hēhē de xiàozhe, mō le mō háizi de tóu.
examples.english: The old man chuckled and patted the child's head.

examples.hanzi: 他只回了我一个呵呵，我也不知道他什么意思。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhǐ huí le wǒ yí gè hēhē, wǒ yě bù zhīdào tā shénme yìsi.
examples.english: He only replied with a 'haha', and I don't know what he meant.

components.note: 石 (stone) — stones and hard things: 研, 码, 砖; 破 is to smash or break.
皮 (pí) is a loose sound clue; same series 坡 pō, 披 pī, 波 bō.
生 (birth) — traditional 產 was 生 (birth) topped by 彦 for sound; the idea is giving birth, so bringing forth, as in 生产 and 产生.

example.hanzi: 那家公司因为经营不善宣布破产。
example.pinyin: Nà jiā gōngsī yīnwèi jīngyíng bùshàn xuānbù pòchǎn.
example.english: That company declared bankruptcy due to poor management.
example.fact: The word 'bankrupt' comes from the Italian banca rotta, meaning 'broken bench,' referring to the practice in medieval Italy of physically breaking a money-lender's table in the marketplace when he could not pay his debts. Modern bankruptcy law traces much of its structure to English statutes from the 16th century, which were originally aimed at punishing debtors rather than helping them recover.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐馆因为疫情破产了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cānguǎn yīnwèi yìqíng pòchǎn le.
examples.english: This restaurant went bankrupt because of the pandemic.

examples.hanzi: 他担心自己的生意会破产。
examples.pinyin: Tā dānxīn zìjǐ de shēngyi huì pòchǎn.
examples.english: He is worried that his business will go bust.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — the plant radical, as in 花 flower and 草 grass; it points to crops and harvest, the sense in 收获. Simplified 获 replaces 獲's left side with 艹.
犾 (dog-like part) — a variant of 犬 dog; 獲 originally meant catching game. Memory aid: grass plus a hunting dog, you bring something home.

example.hanzi: 他在比赛中获得了第一名。
example.pinyin: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng huòdé le dì yī míng.
example.english: He won first place in the competition.
example.fact: 获 is formal and mostly in compounds: 获得 (to obtain), 获奖 (win an award), 收获 (harvest or gain) and 获胜 (win). It originally referred to catching game.

examples.hanzi: 他获得了一份好工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā huòdé le yí fèn hǎo gōngzuò.
examples.english: He landed a good job.

examples.hanzi: 警察成功抓获了小偷。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá chénggōng zhuāhuò le xiǎotōu.
examples.english: The police successfully caught the thief.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 桌, 板: 查 first meant a raft of wood. 查 also gives 渣 zhā and 楂 zhā.
手 (hand) — over 目 (eye): a hand shading the eyes to look into the distance. 目 marks seeing words, as in 眼, 睡.

example.hanzi: 请帮我查看一下这个数据。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ chákàn yíxià zhège shùjù.
example.english: Please help me check this data.
example.fact: The Voyager Golden Record, launched into space in 1977, was designed so that a sufficiently advanced civilization could check its contents using instructions etched onto its cover, including a diagram showing how to build a device to play it and images decoded pixel by pixel. It carried sounds and images meant to represent life and culture on Earth to whoever might one day examine it.

examples.hanzi: 你可以在手机上查看快递的位置。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ zài shǒujī shàng chákàn kuàidì de wèizhi.
examples.english: You can check the parcel's location on your phone.

examples.hanzi: 医生查看了他的检查结果。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng chákàn le tā de jiǎnchá jiéguǒ.
examples.english: The doctor looked over his test results.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 做; 伪 is a person acting a part: fake.
为 (wéi) hints at the sound: 伪 wěi is close.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 造 is to go and make something.
告 (gào) is a loose sound clue (-ao); also in 浩 hào, 靠 kào.

example.hanzi: 有人伪造了他的签名。
example.pinyin: Yǒu rén wěizào le tā de qiānmíng.
example.english: Someone forged his signature.
example.fact: Han van Meegeren, a Dutch painter active in the 1930s and 40s, forged paintings so convincingly attributed to Johannes Vermeer that top art experts of the era authenticated them as genuine, and one was even sold to a senior Nazi official during World War II. Van Meegeren was only caught after the war, when he had to prove the painting was his own forgery to avoid a treason charge for selling Dutch cultural heritage to the enemy.

examples.hanzi: 伪造证件是犯法的。
examples.pinyin: Wěizào zhèngjiàn shì fànfǎ de.
examples.english: Forging documents is against the law.

examples.hanzi: 警察发现这些钞票是伪造的。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá fāxiàn zhèxiē chāopiào shì wěizào de.
examples.english: The police discovered that these banknotes were counterfeit.

meanings: (of a performer) to come onto the stage to perform
(of an athlete) to enter the arena to compete
(fig.) to enter the scene (e.g. a new product)
(of an examinee etc) to leave the venue

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.

example.hanzi: 冠军选手最后一个出场。
example.pinyin: Guànjūn xuǎnshǒu zuìhòu yí gè chūchǎng.
example.english: The champion athlete came out last.
example.fact: At the Olympic Games opening ceremony, the host country's athletes traditionally enter the stadium last, a tradition formalized at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics, while every other nation enters alphabetically according to the host country's language. This order is why viewers often see Greece, home of the ancient Olympics, enter first regardless of the host nation's alphabet.

examples.hanzi: 主角在第二幕才出场。
examples.pinyin: Zhǔjué zài dì-èr mù cái chūchǎng.
examples.english: The lead character only comes on stage in the second act.

examples.hanzi: 他受伤了，今天不能出场比赛。
examples.pinyin: Tā shòushāng le, jīntiān bù néng chūchǎng bǐsài.
examples.english: He is injured and can't play in today's match.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — calling out; 夕 (evening) beside it: in the dark you cannot be seen, so you call your name.
义 (justice, meaning) also lends its sound to 议 yì discuss, 仪 yí ceremony and 蚁 yǐ ant — a useful clue in many characters.

example.hanzi: 这个基金会以帮助贫困儿童的名义筹款。
example.pinyin: Zhège jījīnhuì yǐ bāngzhù pínkùn értóng de míngyì chóukuǎn.
example.english: This foundation raises funds in the name of helping poor children.
example.fact: Many international charities operate under officially registered names that differ from their commonly known public name, a legal structure used to raise funds across borders while satisfying each country's separate registration and tax requirements. Regulatory bodies in most countries require charities to publicly disclose what percentage of donations raised in their name actually reaches program work versus administrative and fundraising costs.

examples.hanzi: 这套房子是以他妻子的名义买的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tào fángzi shì yǐ tā qīzi de míngyì mǎi de.
examples.english: This apartment was bought in his wife's name.

examples.hanzi: 他名义上是经理，其实没什么权力。
examples.pinyin: Tā míngyì shàng shì jīnglǐ, qíshí méi shénme quánlì.
examples.english: He is a manager in name only and actually has little power.

meanings: in the middle of the night

components.note: 半 (half) — 牛 (an ox) divided in two by 八: half. Seen in 一半 half, 半夜 midnight.
夕 (evening) — 夕 is evening or dusk, as in 外, 多, 梦; 夜 is night.
亦 (yì) — near sound — 夜 is yè; 夜 also sounds out 液 yè.

example.hanzi: 他半夜被一阵怪声吵醒了。
example.pinyin: Tā bànyè bèi yí zhèn guài shēng chǎo xǐng le.
example.english: He was woken up at midnight by a strange noise.
example.fact: The convention of starting a new calendar day at midnight rather than at sunrise or sunset, common in many older cultures, became standardized largely through the spread of mechanical clocks in medieval Europe, which could track time evenly through the night rather than relying on daylight. Astronomers, however, traditionally used a system where the day began at noon, a practice that persisted in some astronomical records until the early 20th century, since noon observations of the sun were far easier to make precisely.

examples.hanzi: 半夜下起了大雨。
examples.pinyin: Bànyè xià qǐ le dàyǔ.
examples.english: It started pouring in the middle of the night.

examples.hanzi: 别半夜打电话给我，我要睡觉。
examples.pinyin: Bié bànyè dǎ diànhuà gěi wǒ, wǒ yào shuìjiào.
examples.english: Don't call me in the middle of the night; I need to sleep.

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is the money radical — 财, 贵, 买, 费; betting stakes money.
者 (zhě) — near hint — 赌 is dǔ; 者 also sounds out 堵 dǔ and 都 dū.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.

example.hanzi: 他把所有的钱都输在了赌场里。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ suǒyǒu de qián dōu shū zài le dǔchǎng lǐ.
example.english: He lost all his money at the casino.
example.fact: The word 'casino' comes from the Italian for 'little house,' originally referring to a small country villa or summer house used for social gatherings, long before it came to mean a gambling establishment. The Casino di Venezia, opened in Venice in 1638, is generally considered the oldest continuously run gambling house in the world.

examples.hanzi: 拉斯维加斯有很多大赌场。
examples.pinyin: Lāsīwéijiāsī yǒu hěn duō dà dǔchǎng.
examples.english: Las Vegas has many big casinos.

examples.hanzi: 我朋友从来不去赌场。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ péngyou cónglái bú qù dǔchǎng.
examples.english: My friend never goes to casinos.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a house, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 完; 富 is a house full of goods, hence rich.
畐 (fú) gives the sound: 富 fù is close, as in 福 fú and 副 fù.

example.hanzi: 他家很富，但是他很朴素。
example.pinyin: Tā jiā hěn fù, dànshì tā hěn púsù.
example.english: His family is wealthy, but he is simple.
example.fact: 富 means rich or abundant. 富有 means 'wealthy' or 'rich in', 财富 is wealth, and 富 is also in the name 富士山 (Mount Fuji) and in 富强 'prosperous and strong'. A rich person is 有钱人 in everyday talk.

examples.hanzi: 这个地区的资源很丰富。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dìqū de zīyuán hěn fēngfù.
examples.english: This region's resources are abundant.

examples.hanzi: 他想早点发财致富。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng zǎodiǎn fācái zhìfù.
examples.english: He wants to get rich soon.

components.note: 力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.
气 (air, vapor) — lines of rising vapor or breath. Add water for 汽 steam; seen in 生气 get angry, 空气 air.

example.hanzi: 搬这个箱子需要很大的力气。
example.pinyin: Bān zhège xiāngzi xūyào hěn dà de lìqi.
example.english: Moving this box requires a lot of physical strength.
example.fact: The dung beetle can pull more than 1,000 times its own body weight, giving it, relative to size, one of the strongest grips of any animal on Earth, a feat researchers have linked to competition among males over mates. By comparison, most strength records among large animals, such as elephants, are far less impressive when scaled against body weight.

examples.hanzi: 他力气很大，一个人就能搬动沙发。
examples.pinyin: Tā lìqi hěn dà, yí gè rén jiù néng bāndòng shāfā.
examples.english: He is so strong that he can move the sofa by himself.

examples.hanzi: 跑完步我一点力气都没有了。
examples.pinyin: Pǎo wán bù wǒ yìdiǎn lìqi dōu méiyǒu le.
examples.english: After running, I have no strength left at all.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 拿; 掩 is to cover with the hand.
奄 (yǎn) gives the sound: 掩 yǎn, close to 淹 yān and 腌 yān.
皿 (dish) — marks vessels, as in 盘, 盒, 盆; 盖 is a lid, a cover over a vessel.

example.hanzi: 厚厚的雪掩盖了整个山谷。
example.pinyin: Hòuhòu de xuě yǎngài le zhěnggè shāngǔ.
example.english: The thick snow covered the entire valley.
example.fact: The Chicxulub asteroid impact 66 million years ago threw up enough dust and soot to blanket the atmosphere for years, blocking sunlight and plunging the planet into darkness — a global cover-up of sunlight that scientists believe helped end the age of dinosaurs.

examples.hanzi: 他用笑容掩盖了内心的紧张。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng xiàoróng yǎngài le nèixīn de jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: He covered up his inner nervousness with a smile.

examples.hanzi: 这件事的真相不可能永远被掩盖。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì de zhēnxiàng bù kěnéng yǒngyuǎn bèi yǎngài.
examples.english: The truth of this matter can't be covered up forever.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a public building where officials work; 官 is an official.
官 (guān) gives the sound of 管 guǎn, 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.
司 (sī) is a sound clue for 词 cí and 饲 sì; as a word it means to manage, as in 公司 company.

example.hanzi: 他们为了这块地打了好几年官司。
example.pinyin: Tāmen wèile zhè kuài dì dǎle hǎo jǐ nián guānsi.
example.english: They fought a lawsuit over this piece of land for several years.
example.fact: The Code of Hammurabi, carved onto a stone stele around 1754 BC, is one of the oldest surviving sets of written laws, and it already included detailed rules for resolving property disputes and contracts — showing that formal legal proceedings are almost as old as writing itself.

examples.hanzi: 他们俩因为遗产打起了官司。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen liǎ yīnwèi yíchǎn dǎ qǐ le guānsi.
examples.english: The two of them got into a lawsuit over the inheritance.

examples.hanzi: 这场官司他赢了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng guānsi tā yíng le.
examples.english: He won this lawsuit.

meanings: Tonkin (northern Vietnam during the French colonial period)

components.note: 东 (east) — simplified from 東; a common memory aid is the sun 日 caught in a tree 木 at sunrise.
京 (jīng) — capital, drawn as a tall building on a mound; as a part it sounds out 景 jǐng, 惊 jīng, 鲸 jīng and 凉 liáng.

example.hanzi: 他下个月要去东京旅行。
example.pinyin: Tā xià gè yuè yào qù Dōngjīng lǚxíng.
example.english: He is going to travel to Tokyo next month.
example.fact: Tokyo's greater metropolitan area is home to roughly 37 million people, making it the most populous metropolitan area on Earth. The city was called Edo until 1868, when it was renamed Tokyo, meaning 'eastern capital,' after the emperor moved the seat of government there from Kyoto.

examples.hanzi: 东京的地铁非常方便，但是很拥挤。
examples.pinyin: Dōngjīng de dìtiě fēicháng fāngbiàn, dànshì hěn yōngjǐ.
examples.english: The subway in Tokyo is very convenient but crowded.

examples.hanzi: 东京的樱花在三月底开放。
examples.pinyin: Dōngjīng de yīnghuā zài sān yuè dǐ kāifàng.
examples.english: Cherry blossoms in Tokyo bloom at the end of March.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.
夕 (evening) — 夕 is evening or dusk, as in 外, 多, 梦; 夜 is night.
亦 (yì) — near sound — 夜 is yè; 夜 also sounds out 液 yè.

example.hanzi: 我们决定在山上的小屋过夜。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen juédìng zài shān shàng de xiǎowū guòyè.
example.english: We decided to spend the night in the cabin on the mountain.
example.fact: In towns above the Arctic Circle, like Utqiagvik, Alaska, the sun can stay below the horizon for over 60 consecutive days each winter — turning an ordinary night into a stretch of darkness lasting more than two months.

examples.hanzi: 你可以在我家过夜，不用回酒店了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ zài wǒ jiā guòyè, búyòng huí jiǔdiàn le.
examples.english: You can stay the night at my place; no need to go back to the hotel.

examples.hanzi: 过夜的饭菜最好别再吃了。
examples.pinyin: Guòyè de fàncài zuì hǎo bié zài chī le.
examples.english: It's best not to eat food that has been left overnight.

components.note: 立 (stand) — a person standing on the ground line. As a radical it appears in 站 stand, 位 seat, 竟; also in 建立 establish.

example.hanzi: 请大家立正站好。
example.pinyin: Qǐng dàjiā lìzhèng zhàn hǎo.
example.english: Everyone please stand at attention.
example.fact: 立 is the base for 立刻 (immediately), 成立 (to found), 独立 (independent) and 立场 (standpoint). In the solar calendar 立春 (start of spring) and 立秋 begin the seasons.

examples.hanzi: 路口立着一块牌子。
examples.pinyin: Lùkǒu lì zhe yí kuài páizi.
examples.english: A sign stands at the intersection.

examples.hanzi: 公司是去年成立的。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī shì qùnián chénglì de.
examples.english: The company was founded last year.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.

example.hanzi: 他的老毛病突然发作了。
example.pinyin: Tā de lǎomáobìng tūrán fāzuò le.
example.english: His old illness suddenly flared up.
example.fact: Solar flares are sudden bursts of radiation from the Sun's surface that can release as much energy in minutes as billions of hydrogen bombs. The most powerful one on record, the 1859 Carrington Event, was strong enough to set telegraph wires on fire and produce auroras visible near the equator.

examples.hanzi: 他的哮喘病在半夜发作了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xiàochuǎn bìng zài bànyè fāzuò le.
examples.english: His asthma flared up in the middle of the night.

examples.hanzi: 他气得想发作，但又忍住了。
examples.pinyin: Tā qì de xiǎng fāzuò, dàn yòu rěn zhù le.
examples.english: He was so angry he wanted to blow up, but held himself back.

components.note: 人 (person) — the right-hand part. The left part is a hook-and-dot, from an old tool-like shape. Meaning 'by means of, so as to' is not shown by the parts today.
Memory aid: a person 人 using a tool to get something done — 'by means of' (可以, 所以, 以前). A mnemonic, not proven etymology.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 以上就是我们今天讨论的内容。
example.pinyin: Yǐshàng jiùshì wǒmen jīntiān tǎolùn de nèiróng.
example.english: The above is what we discussed today.
example.fact: Mount Everest's summit sits 8,849 meters above sea level, an altitude close to the cruising height of early jet airliners before pressurized cabins became standard. The mountain is still slowly rising a few millimeters a year as the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates keep colliding.

examples.hanzi: 十八岁以上的人才可以进入。
examples.pinyin: Shíbā suì yǐshàng de rén cái kěyǐ jìnrù.
examples.english: Only people aged eighteen and above can enter.

examples.hanzi: 以上这些问题，请大家认真考虑。
examples.pinyin: Yǐshàng zhèxiē wèntí, qǐng dàjiā rènzhēn kǎolǜ.
examples.english: Please think carefully about the questions above.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 挑 is to pick out by hand.
兆 (zhào) is a loose sound clue; same part in 跳 tiào, 桃 táo and 逃 táo.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 进: to go and pick.
先 (xiān) is a close sound clue for xuǎn; 先 also in 洗 xǐ.

example.hanzi: 她花了很长时间挑选礼物。
example.pinyin: Tā huāle hěn cháng shíjiān tiāoxuǎn lǐwù.
example.english: She spent a long time choosing a gift.
example.fact: Natural selection, the mechanism Charles Darwin proposed in 1859, works by favoring individuals whose inherited traits happen to fit their environment. Over many generations this quietly 'selects' which genes get passed on, without any conscious choice ever being involved.

examples.hanzi: 你喜欢哪个，自己挑选吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan nǎge, zìjǐ tiāoxuǎn ba.
examples.english: Pick whichever one you like.

examples.hanzi: 教练从二十个人里挑选了十个队员。
examples.pinyin: Jiàoliàn cóng èrshí gè rén lǐ tiāoxuǎn le shí gè duìyuán.
examples.english: The coach selected ten players out of twenty.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — boundaries: 国, 园, 围; 团 is a round group. Its traditional form had 專 as sound, like 转 zhuǎn and 传 chuán.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and ties, as in 红, 给, 经; 结 is a knot.
吉 (jí) is a close sound clue for jié; 吉 also sounds out 洁 jié.

example.hanzi: 全体队员必须团结起来才能赢。
example.pinyin: Quántǐ duìyuán bìxū tuánjié qǐlái cáinéng yíng.
example.english: All the team members must unite in order to win.
example.fact: Emperor penguins in Antarctica huddle together in tightly packed groups of thousands, rotating positions so every bird gets a turn sheltered from the wind at the center. This cooperative strategy can raise the temperature inside the huddle to nearly 37°C even when it is -40°C outside.

examples.hanzi: 团结就是力量。
examples.pinyin: Tuánjié jiù shì lìliang.
examples.english: Unity is strength.

examples.hanzi: 我们班同学之间非常团结。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bān tóngxué zhījiān fēicháng tuánjié.
examples.english: The students in our class are very united.

components.note: 阝 on the left is 阜 (steps, hill) — as in 院, 阳, 阴: 除 first meant palace steps; to step away, remove.
余 (yú) is a loose sound clue for chú; 余 also in 涂 tú, 途 tú and 徐 xú.
扌 (hand) — hand radical for actions — 掉 is to drop or lose hold.

example.hanzi: 农民想办法除掉田里的害虫。
example.pinyin: Nóngmín xiǎng bànfǎ chúdiào tián lǐ de hàichóng.
example.english: The farmer tried to find a way to eliminate the pests in the field.
example.fact: Smallpox is the only human disease ever fully eradicated worldwide, declared eliminated by the World Health Organization in 1980 after a global vaccination campaign that lasted more than a decade.

examples.hanzi: 怎样才能除掉衣服上的污渍？
examples.pinyin: Zěnyàng cáinéng chúdiào yīfu shàng de wūzì?
examples.english: How can I get the stain off my clothes?

examples.hanzi: 他想除掉这个坏习惯。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng chúdiào zhège huài xíguàn.
examples.english: He wants to get rid of this bad habit.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions taken on something: 教, 放, 改; 救 is to take action to rescue.
求 (qiú) is a near sound match for jiù; 求 also means ask for help.
扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 援 is to lend a hand.
爰 (yuán) gives the sound exactly: 援 yuán, also in 暖 nuǎn and 缓 huǎn.

example.hanzi: 救援队连夜赶到了灾区。
example.pinyin: Jiùyuán duì liányè gǎndào le zāiqū.
example.english: The rescue team rushed to the disaster area overnight.
example.fact: The 2010 rescue of 33 Chilean miners trapped half a mile underground at the San José mine took 69 days and required drilling an entirely new escape shaft. All 33 men survived, making it one of the most successful mine rescues in history.

examples.hanzi: 消防队员正在全力救援被困的人。
examples.pinyin: Xiāofáng duìyuán zhèngzài quánlì jiùyuán bèi kùn de rén.
examples.english: Firefighters are doing everything to rescue the trapped people.

examples.hanzi: 救援工作进行得很顺利。
examples.pinyin: Jiùyuán gōngzuò jìnxíng de hěn shùnlì.
examples.english: The rescue work is going smoothly.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving — 速 is speed, as in 快速 and 速度.
束 (shù) — near sound — 速 is sù, same syllable with different initial.

example.hanzi: 汽车的速度很快。
example.pinyin: Qìchē de sùdù hěn kuài.
example.english: The car's speed is very fast.
example.fact: 速 is formal: 速度 (speed), 快速 (rapid), 高速 (high-speed), and 高速公路 is an expressway. In Taiwan, 速食 is 'fast food' where the mainland says 快餐.

examples.hanzi: 高速公路上车很多。
examples.pinyin: Gāosù gōnglù shang chē hěn duō.
examples.english: There's a lot of traffic on the highway.

examples.hanzi: 他说话的语速很快。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuōhuà de yǔsù hěn kuài.
examples.english: He speaks very fast.

components.note: 足 (foot) — 足 (⻊) marks feet and body positions, as in 跑, 跳, 路; 趴 is lying on the front.
八 (bā) — same sound — 趴 is pā; 八 is bā, like 扒 bā and 叭 bā.

example.hanzi: 他趴在桌子上睡着了。
example.pinyin: Tā pā zài zhuōzi shàng shuìzháo le.
example.english: He fell asleep lying on the desk.
example.fact: 趴 describes lying face-down or leaning your upper body on something: 趴着睡 is sleeping on one's stomach. In the command 趴下! it means 'get down!'. Taiwan also uses 趴 for 'percent'.

examples.hanzi: 小猫趴在窗台上晒太阳。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo māo pā zài chuāngtái shang shài tàiyáng.
examples.english: The kitten lies on the windowsill sunbathing.

examples.hanzi: 他趴在地上做俯卧撑。
examples.pinyin: Tā pā zài dì shang zuò fǔwòchēng.
examples.english: He's doing push-ups on the ground.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.

example.hanzi: 这个故事的开头非常吸引人。
example.pinyin: Zhège gùshì de kāitóu fēicháng xīyǐn rén.
example.english: The beginning of this story is very engaging.
example.fact: The Big Bang theory holds that the observable universe began expanding from an extremely hot, dense state roughly 13.8 billion years ago. The faint microwave radiation left over from that beginning, the cosmic microwave background, can still be detected filling all of space today.

examples.hanzi: 万事开头难，坚持下去就好了。
examples.pinyin: Wànshì kāitóu nán, jiānchí xiàqù jiù hǎo le.
examples.english: Every beginning is hard, but it gets better if you keep at it.

examples.hanzi: 这封信的开头是这样写的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fēng xìn de kāitóu shì zhèyàng xiě de.
examples.english: The letter begins like this.

components.note: 民 (people) — one old theory sees an eye pierced by a pointed tool, a mark of those with no rights; the meaning "ordinary people" is what to remember.

example.hanzi: 这个国家的人民很友好。
example.pinyin: Zhège guójiā de rénmín hěn yǒuhǎo.
example.english: The people of this country are very friendly.
example.fact: 民 is bound in compounds like 人民 (the people), 国民 (citizens), 居民 (residents) and 民族 (ethnic group). The proverb 民以食为天 says that 'food is heaven to the people'.

examples.hanzi: 这座城市有一千万居民。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì yǒu yì qiān wàn jūmín.
examples.english: This city has ten million residents.

examples.hanzi: 农民们在田里忙着收麦子。
examples.pinyin: Nóngmínmen zài tián li máng zhe shōu màizi.
examples.english: The farmers are busy harvesting wheat in the field.

components.note: 羽 (feather, wing) — marks wings and flight, as in 翅 wing, 翔 soar; 翘 is lifting up like wings, as in 翘起.
尧 (yáo) — close sound: 翘 qiáo. 尧 also sounds out 烧 shāo and 晓 xiǎo.

example.hanzi: 小狗的尾巴翘得高高的。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu de wěiba qiào de gāogāo de.
example.english: The puppy's tail is sticking up high.
example.fact: 翘 has two readings: qiào, 'to curl up, warp' (翘课 means 'to skip class') and qiáo, 'to raise', as in 翘二郎腿 ('cross one's legs') or 翘首 ('to crane one's neck'). 翘楚 means an outstanding person.

examples.hanzi: 他的头发睡觉后翘起来了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de tóufa shuìjiào hòu qiào qǐlái le.
examples.english: His hair stuck up after he slept.

examples.hanzi: 木板被太阳晒翘了。
examples.pinyin: Mùbǎn bèi tàiyáng shài qiào le.
examples.english: The board warped in the sun.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
木 (wood) — trees and wooden things: 树, 板, 样; 模 was a wooden mold or pattern.
莫 (mò) is close to mó; same part in 摸 mō, 膜 mó, 墓 mù.
一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌 table, 板 board; 样 once meant a tree (acorn) and later "form, pattern".
羊 (yáng, sheep) is a near-exact sound clue for yàng; 羊 also sounds out 洋 yáng and 养 yǎng.

example.hanzi: 这两件衣服看起来一模一样。
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng jiàn yīfu kàn qǐlái yīmúyīyàng.
example.english: These two pieces of clothing look exactly alike.
example.fact: Identical twins form when a single fertilized egg splits into two embryos early in development, so they share nearly 100% of their DNA. Yet even genetically identical twins raised together develop distinct fingerprints, because those patterns form partly from random pressure differences inside the womb.

examples.hanzi: 双胞胎长得一模一样，连妈妈都分不清。
examples.pinyin: Shuāngbāotāi zhǎng de yìmúyíyàng, lián māma dōu fēn bù qīng.
examples.english: The twins look exactly alike, and even their mom can't tell them apart.

examples.hanzi: 你的包和我的一模一样。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de bāo hé wǒ de yìmúyíyàng.
examples.english: Your bag is exactly the same as mine.

components.note: 入 (enter) — a pointed shape pushing in; not 人 (person), whose strokes spread outward.
口 (mouth) — a picture of an open mouth; as a radical it appears in characters of speech, eating and sounds — 吃, 喝, 叫, 吗.

example.hanzi: 博物馆的入口在大楼的东边。
example.pinyin: Bówùguǎn de rùkǒu zài dàlóu de dōngbian.
example.english: The museum's entrance is on the east side of the building.
example.fact: The entrance to Carlsbad Caverns in New Mexico is famous for the hundreds of thousands of bats that spiral out of it every summer evening at dusk, a nightly exodus that can take over an hour to complete.

examples.hanzi: 请问，地铁站的入口在哪儿？
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, dìtiězhàn de rùkǒu zài nǎr?
examples.english: Excuse me, where is the entrance to the subway station?

examples.hanzi: 我在公园入口等你。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài gōngyuán rùkǒu děng nǐ.
examples.english: I'll wait for you at the park entrance.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: receiving something by hand.
妾 (qiè) is only a loose sound clue for jiē.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 新经理接手了这个项目。
example.pinyin: Xīn jīnglǐ jiēshǒu le zhège xiàngmù.
example.english: The new manager took over this project.
example.fact: When Steve Jobs returned to lead Apple in 1997 after being ousted twelve years earlier, the company was reportedly only weeks away from bankruptcy. Within a few years of him taking over again, it launched the iMac and later the iPod.

examples.hanzi: 他刚接手这家店，还不太熟悉。
examples.pinyin: Tā gāng jiēshǒu zhè jiā diàn, hái bú tài shúxī.
examples.english: He just took over this shop and isn't familiar with it yet.

examples.hanzi: 我走了以后，谁来接手我的工作？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zǒu le yǐhòu, shéi lái jiēshǒu wǒ de gōngzuò?
examples.english: After I leave, who will take over my work?

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 改, 放: to gather by force or hand.
丩 (jiū) is only a loose sound clue for shōu.
手 (hand) — over 目 (eye): a hand shading the eyes to look into the distance. 目 marks seeing words, as in 眼, 睡.

example.hanzi: 很多人收看了昨晚的比赛直播。
example.pinyin: Hěnduō rén shōukàn le zuówǎn de bǐsài zhíbò.
example.english: Many people watched last night's live broadcast of the game.
example.fact: The 1969 Apollo 11 moon landing was watched live on television by an estimated 600 million people worldwide — roughly one in every six people alive at the time — making it one of the most-viewed broadcasts in history.

examples.hanzi: 感谢您收看今天的节目。
examples.pinyin: Gǎnxiè nín shōukàn jīntiān de jiémù.
examples.english: Thank you for watching today's program.

examples.hanzi: 爷爷每天晚上都收看新闻。
examples.pinyin: Yéye měi tiān wǎnshang dōu shōukàn xīnwén.
examples.english: Grandpa watches the news every evening.

components.note: 阝 on the left is 阜 (mound, hill) — as in 院, 阳, 阴: a steep place, a risky pass.
佥 (qiān) is a loose sound clue for xiǎn; 佥 also in 检 jiǎn, 剑 jiàn, 脸 liǎn and 验 yàn.

example.hanzi: 这条山路很危险。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo shānlù hěn wēixiǎn.
example.english: This mountain road is very dangerous.
example.fact: 险 builds 危险 (dangerous), 保险 (insurance, literally 'guarantee against danger') and 探险 (to explore). 险些 / 险 as an adverb means 'nearly, narrowly', as in 险些摔倒 'nearly fell'.

examples.hanzi: 爬山很有风险。
examples.pinyin: Páshān hěn yǒu fēngxiǎn.
examples.english: Mountain climbing is risky.

examples.hanzi: 我们买了旅游保险。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen mǎi le lǚyóu bǎoxiǎn.
examples.english: We bought travel insurance.
